title: The Benefit Design a Sponsor Buys in the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans
content:
A group retiree plan pays on the benefit design the sponsor bought, which is ordinarily richer than the plans sold to individuals and always differs from them. Every plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans is written on that footing.

## A medical group plan

A medical group plan pays at the in-network cost share wherever the retiree lives, at any provider who accepts Medicare, which is why retirees who move are still covered on the same terms.

## A drug-only employer group waiver plan

A drug-only employer group waiver plan carries no medical benefit at all, and a retiree of such a group keeps Original Medicare or another medical plan for their medical care.

## Drug coverage above the standard benefit

Where the sponsor bought wrap coverage the plan pays above the standard Part D benefit, so a retiree's drug costs may look nothing like what an individual plan would charge.

## Benefits the sponsor chose, and benefits it did not

Supplemental benefits such as dental, vision, fitness and the allowance card are the sponsor's choice, and a retiree asking for one their group did not buy is told plainly that their employer did not include it rather than that the plan does not offer it.

## Coverage decisions and appeals

Coverage decisions and appeals follow the same deadlines as any Medicare Advantage plan, and a group retiree has exactly the same appeal rights as anybody else.

## Points of judgement

The design is bought by the sponsor, so what one retiree of this book is entitled to is settled by the plan their own sponsor bought and not by what another retiree of another group holds.

Whether a retiree on a drug-only employer group waiver plan is covered for a medical service is not a question about that plan at all, since it carries no medical benefit; it is a question about the Original Medicare or other medical plan that retiree keeps.

Where a supplemental benefit is absent, it is absent because the sponsor did not buy it, not because the plan has none to give.
